anti_duplication_rules: All jurisdiction package YAML/JSON loading goes through packages/jurisdiction_knowledge_packages/schema.py:load_package_manifest; do not add ad hoc YAML parsing in CLI, compiler, lifecycle, or tests.
All package validation goes through packages/jurisdiction_knowledge_packages/validation.py:validate_package; do not duplicate protected-control checks in command wrappers or migration files.

All package, evidence, artifact, diff, and drift digests go through packages/jurisdiction_knowledge_packages/digests.py using packages/svs_common/svs_common/hashing.py primitives; do not hand-roll JSON string hashing elsewhere.

Compiled experts must enter packages/svs_common/svs_common/expert_profiles.py:EXPERT_PROFILE_REGISTRY or its existing composition path; package manifests are declarative source inputs and are not a second runtime registry.

Compiled search lenses must enter packages/svs_common/svs_common/search_lenses.py:SEARCH_LENS_REGISTRY or its existing composition path; do not duplicate graph/search lens selection, query planning, or graph expansion logic in package files.

Kansas Court Decisions and Topeka Municipal Code profile definitions must have one authoritative declarative package manifest each; do not hand-maintain duplicate Kansas or Topeka profile definitions in both YAML and Python.

Generated draft content may include package declarations, descriptions, eval candidates, and provenance only; it must not contain tenancy, RLS, scopes, citation authority activation, provider routing, security routing, memory authority, output guards, or tool ceilings.

Draft generation must use packages/svs_common/svs_common/expert_llm.py and the model gateway boundary; no direct OpenAI, Anthropic, local provider, or provider SDK import is allowed in packages/jurisdiction_knowledge_packages/drafting.py.

Package lifecycle state is owned only by packages/jurisdiction_knowledge_packages/lifecycle.py; audit.py may render lifecycle records but must not write a separate audit store, status file, or activation marker.
No package command may autoactivate a generated draft; promote, rollback, and deactivate require explicit operator CLI subcommands, a valid package digest, and lifecycle event recording.

Reference migrations must preserve existing caller-facing expert IDs, vector store IDs, graph lens IDs, and route behavior; any renaming requires an explicit compatibility shim in the existing registry owner.

Do not include or depend on any external vendor-reference path from enrichment in implementation, file_modification_map, manifests, imports, tests, or docs; prior vendor inspection remains reference-only.

tickets.expected_output: A new jurisdiction package schema and typed loader can express all required corpus families and reports corpus-type-specific missing sections through validate_package.
Package validation emits evidence identifiers, evidence digests, artifact digests, and a stable canonical package digest that changes when declarations or source evidence change.

Valid package expert declarations compile into existing ExpertProfileDefinition-compatible entries consumed by the current expert profile resolver without a parallel runtime registry or caller ID changes.

Validation fails closed on protected runtime controls in package manifests or generated drafts, while tests prove runtime-owned scope, RLS, provider, memory, citation, guard, and tool-limit controls remain external constraints.
Corpus types declare connector, metadata, chunking, graph, search, caveat, and eval extension descriptors through typed contracts without per-jurisdiction compiler branches.
Package graph/search descriptors compile into the existing search lens/query-planner/API routing surfaces, preserving specialized graph-backed behavior without duplicated graph expansion code.
The shared jurisdiction-package CLI can scaffold an inactive package directory with manifest, corpus cards, expert declarations, eval stubs, and docs placeholders that pass structural validation.

The generate command builds inactive draft package content from bounded store metadata, capability descriptors, and representative retrieval evidence through the model gateway boundary with provenance and no protected controls.

Operators get deterministic validate and diff commands with machine-readable diagnostics, nonzero failure exits, digest changes, protected-control violations, and compile-result reporting without mutation during validation.
Promote, rollback, and deactivate commands require an already-valid package digest, write lifecycle/audit events through lifecycle.py, and never activate generated drafts implicitly.

The drift command compares promoted package state, corpus evidence digests, compiler outputs, and current server-owned store metadata, reporting unchanged, changed, missing, and stale states with deterministic exits.

Kansas Court Decisions is represented as a reference package that compiles into unchanged expert/vector-store/search IDs with passing semantic search, graph, expert, follow-up, and citation-support regression checks.

Topeka Municipal Code is represented as a reference package that compiles into unchanged expert/vector-store/search IDs with passing code, ordinance-history, graph, expert, follow-up, and citation-support regression checks.
Focused deterministic tests prove schema validation, stable digests, fail-closed protected controls, compiler registry output, lifecycle transitions, drift reporting, and both reference migrations.

Documented Docker/live proof commands exercise both reference packages end to end for semantic retrieval, graph behavior, search tools, expert routing, follow-up, and citation support, without relying on GitHub CI as the only gate.

README, playbook, caller docs, and runbooks describe scaffold, generate, validate, diff, promote, rollback, deactivate, drift, proof collection, and protected-control boundaries for new ExAIS instances.
